insights.title: Downpours are becoming more common
insights.body: Days with 20 mm or more of rain went from about 23 to 28 a year (first vs last 10 years). Bare soil during these storms washes away fastest.

insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 811 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Rice, Salt-tolerant rice and Maize score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: More downpours: about 34 heavy-rain days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Up from about 25 today. Each downpour on bare soil washes away topsoil and the fertiliser in it; fields here are barest in May.
consequences.action: Keep the ground covered (a legume or crop residue) through the rainy months.

consequences.headline: +0.5 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 27.4 °C to about 27.9 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
